papers.title: Experimental trophic flexibility guides a compartmentalized genome-scale model of red microalgae Galdieria sulphuraria
papers.abstract: The thermoacidophilic red microalga Galdieria sulphuraria combines broad organic-carbon utilization with biotechnological robustness. We integrated cultivation data for strain SAG 107.79 with an organelle-resolved genome-scale metabolic model describing autotrophic, mixotrophic and heterotrophic metabolism. Heterotrophic cultures produced 2.29, 2.03 and 2.14 g L-1 biomass on glucose, xylose and their mixture, respectively, while mixed-sugar cultures consumed glucose before xylose. Biomass composition was similar under mixotrophy and heterotrophy, and stationary-phase glucose consumption supported a non-growth-associated maintenance demand of 1.7 mmol ATP gDW-1 h-1. These measurements informed trophic-state-specific biomass objective functions. The final model contains 2,487 reactions, 2,270 compartment-specific metabolites and 1,050 genes. The model reproduced the experimentally scored growth phenotypes, highlighted polyol-associated product capacity under heterotrophy and scored 90% in the archived MEMOTE report. To our knowledge, this is the first experimentally based, organelle-resolved genome-scale metabolic model for G. sulphuraria, providing a quantitative framework linking trophic state and substrate identity with carbon use, flux flexibility and product capacity. A user-friendly supplementary package provides the executable SBML model, modular biomass resources, reproducible scripts, quality reports and underlying experimental data.

papers.title: Drug-centric knowledge graph: representing therapeutic modality, pharmacology and multiscale biology
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs link targets to mechanisms, diseases and phenotypes, but target-centered representations omit much of what distinguishes therapeutic interventions. We introduce a drug-centric knowledge graph, whose identity model, schema and information-selection priorities are organized around the therapeutic intervention, and a graph built on this design. Each intervention has one identity, linked through relation types shared by all compounds, including target actions, indications, adverse effects, classifications, half-life and direct links to pathways, Gene Ontology concepts, cells and anatomy, and through modality-specific relation types describing small-molecule chemistry, antibody sequences and formats, protein-therapy sequences and antibody-drug conjugate components. Integrating 38 source resources, the graph contains 166,261 nodes of 27 types, 8,106,906 directed edges of 129 relation types and 18,429 compounds in eight therapeutic categories. Construction combines source-specific extraction, compound-identity resolution, language-model-assisted vocabulary and predicate mapping, confidence scoring and connectivity filtering; an expert-reviewed workflow adds investigational therapeutics without altering the base graph. The design offers a reusable template for representing interventions as structured, multimodal objects.

papers.title: Root responses to mechanical heterogeneity are shaped by pore geometry and root-soil biomechanics
papers.abstract: Mechanical limitations to root growth occur when pressure exerted by turgor within root cells is counteracted by excessive resistance of the surrounding soil as well as by that of the cell walls. In a natural soil, however, heterogeneity allows roots to find paths of least resistance, though the governing principles behind this process have yet to be identified. Here, we combined artificial substrates, high-throughput live imaging, advanced image analysis, and mechanical modelling to uncover the principles governing the ability of a root to penetrate or deflect from zones of high mechanical impedance within a heterogeneous substrate. Our findings show that root responses to substrate heterogeneity can be accurately predicted from the pore-matrix geometry when both the mechanical properties of the substrate and those of the roots are known. Consequently, a crucial step toward understanding the physical limitations to root growth may lie in a detailed characterisation of soil mechanical properties.

papers.title: Targeting proteasome composition reprograms tumor-intrinsic inflammation through selective degradation of STAT1
papers.abstract: Proteasome regulatory particles determine cellular protein degradation capacities. Yet specific ubiquitin-independent degradation targets of individual proteasome regulatory particles, and physiological roles of such pathways, remain largely elusive. Here, through a chemical biology-driven approach, we identify a covalent small molecule that selectively targets a conformationally dynamic pocket in the non-catalytic proteasome regulator PSME4 and modulates tumor cell proteasome targets. Using this chemical probe together with orthogonal genetic perturbations, we show that blocking or reducing PSME4 stabilizes STAT1, restores interferon-associated transcription, enhances antigen presentation, and disrupts IL-6/STAT3 signaling, collectively reprogramming tumor inflammation and suppressing tumor growth in vivo. These findings define a PSME4-STAT1-STAT3 axis that couples proteasomal degradation to antigen presentation and cytokine signaling and provide a framework for pharmacologically targeting non-catalytic proteasome regulators to reprogram tumor immunity. More broadly, our findings reveal that proteasome composition can actively govern the balance between immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive signaling programs.

papers.title: Spatial protein quality control requires a functional GET pathway to prevent proteotoxicity
papers.abstract: The proper management of misfolded proteins is an essential biological process that is required for the survival of all organisms. Previous work has demonstrated that misfolded proteins can be spatially sequestered into membrane-less compartments to facilitate their degradation. Soluble cytoplasmic misfolded proteins are sequestered in the juxtanuclear quality control compartment (JUNQ), and insoluble cytoplasmic misfolded proteins are sequestered into the insoluble protein deposit (IPOD). It is still unknown if there are upstream targeting pathways necessary for regulating JUNQ and IPOD formation. Here we investigated the role of ER targeting on JUNQ and IPOD formation. We find that the GET pathway is necessary for JUNQ formation. Inefficiencies in the GET pathway contribute to premature IPOD formation, and a defective GET pathway inhibits JUNQ formation altogether. Notably, we find the role of the GET pathway in JUNQ formation is required for cell survival and loss of GET pathway function is only toxic under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we identify a new role for the GET pathway in regulating spatial PQC and demonstrate that spatial quality control is essential for cell health and survival.

papers.title: Interleukin-4 suppresses TIMP-2 transcription during endometriosis: Allele-specific regulation of the TIMP-2 -418G/C promoter by SP1
papers.abstract: Abstract Tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-2 (TIMP-2) is a critical regulator of extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis in inflammatory disorder, but the mechanisms underlying its dysregulation in endometriosis remain poorly understood. Furthermore, whether inflammatory cytokine signaling and functional genetic variants within the TIMP-2 promoter contribute to its altered expression during disease progression is unknown. This study investigated the regulation of TIMP-2 expression by interleukin-4 (IL-4) signaling and the functional significance of the TIMP-2 -418G/C promoter polymorphism in endometriosis. We found that TIMP-2 expression was significantly reduced in ectopic lesions and serum samples from endometriosis patients in comparison to normal. Functional promoter analyses revealed that the -418C allele exhibited higher basal transcriptional activity than the G allele while displayed greater sensitivity to IL-4-mediated repression. IL-4 activated STAT6 signaling concomitant with SP1 and TIMP-2 downregulation, whereas SP1 overexpression restored TIMP-2 expression and SP1 silencing further suppressed its transcription, identifying SP1 as a positive regulator of TIMP-2. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses identified fibroblasts and mesenchymal populations as the major TIMP-2-expressing cell types and revealed enhanced inflammatory signaling and ECM remodeling networks in endometriosis. Collectively, these findings identify an IL-4-SP1-TIMP-2 regulatory axis that contributes to aberrant ECM turnover in endometriosis. Furthermore, the TIMP-2 -418G/C promoter polymorphism influences cytokine-mediated transcriptional regulation of TIMP-2, providing new mechanistic insights into the interplay between inflammatory signaling, genetic variation, and ECM homeostasis during endometriosis progression.

papers.title: Synthetic biology-guided modular engineering of the secreted cutinase FoCut5a with a carbohydrate-binding module improves poly(ester-urethane) depolymerization in Yarrowia lipolytica
papers.abstract: Poly(ester-urethane) bioconversion requires efficient polymer-degrading enzymes and microbial hosts capable of processing the resulting monomers. However, the optimal modular design of secreted cutinases for depolymerizing insoluble polyester-polyurethanes remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a combinatorial synthetic biology strategy in Yarrowia lipolytica based on the fungal cutinase FoCut5a from Fusarium oxysporum. A library of 96 Golden Gate-assembled constructs, combining four secretion signals, four interdomain linkers, and six substrate-binding domains, was integrated site-specifically into the genome and screened for depolymerization of the polyester-polyurethane dispersion Impranil DLN-SD. The best-performing variant fused FoCut5a to the carbohydrate-binding module TrCBM1. LC-MS analysis demonstrated release of adipic acid, 1,6-hexanediol, and neopentyl glycol, confirming ester-bond hydrolysis within the polyester domains of the polymer and additionally detected 6-hydroxycaproate, indicating oxidation of polyurethane-derived 1,6-hexanediol by Y. lipolytica. Purified FoCut5a-TrCBM1 displayed unchanged activity on p-nitrophenyl butyrate but reduced Impranil turbidity 5.6-fold faster and increased release of 1,6-hexanediol and adipic acid by 76-fold and 220-fold, respectively, compared to the unfused enzyme. These results highlight modular enzyme engineering as an effective strategy to enhance polyester-polyurethane deconstruction and support Y. lipolytica as a platform for polymer bioconversion and upcycling.

papers.title: First report on chromosome number and genome size of rare endemic birch Betula klokovii Zaverucha from Ukraine
papers.abstract: This study presents the first report on chromosome number and genome size estimate for rare endemic birch species Betula klokovii Zaverucha from Ukraine. Karyological analysis of metaphases revealed a total of 56 chromosomes, confirming a tetraploid cytotype (2n = 4x = 56). Concurrently, flow cytometry (FCM) was utilized to conduct a precise genome estimation, yielding a nuclear DNA content of 2C = 1.93-1.99 pg for fresh material and 2.15-2.53 pg for herbarium. In addition, we identified one seedling with lower DNA content of 2C = 1.46 pg that most likely corresponds to F1 triploid hybrid between B. klokovii and B. pendula Roth. The results contribute significantly to our understanding of genomic evolution within the genus Betula L. and provide important insights into the taxonomy and conservation genetics of rare European birch taxa.

papers.title: Genomic signals of local adaptation in UK black alder populations (Alnus glutinosa)
papers.abstract: Black alder (Alnus glutinosa) is a native tree species in the British Isles, which it colonised after the last glaciation from continental refugia. It is now a widespread pioneer species, thriving on wetlands and riverbanks. We present whole genome sequence data for 324 alder seedlings grown from seed collected from 44 populations across the UK. Among these we found two triploids and one sample with trisomy at chromosome five. Removing these, we found little population genetic structure apart from diverging northern populations with lower diversity. Using Latent-Factor Mixed Models (LFMM) analyses we identified 1,364 loci whose allele frequencies were significantly associated with environmental variables. Of these loci, 93% were associated with the number of snow days. In contrast, the greatest total genomic signal (variance in SNP effect sizes of 7.38 million SNP loci) was observed for mean temperature of the wettest quarter and annual number of frost days. Estimates of maladaptation using 1.49 million SNPs, predicted that northern populations are worst adapted to present and future worst-case climates. Our results suggest that similarity of source-site temperature variables should be prioritised when choosing seed sources for new planting, and northern populations could benefit from assisted gene flow from the south.

papers.title: Grazing versus mowing: productivity and forage quality of mixtures and cultivars of perennial ryegrass
papers.abstract: Perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne L.) is an important grass species in temporary grasslands, where it is often sown as a mixture of multiple cultivars. In variety testing, however, candidate cultivars are evaluated as single-cultivar stands under standardised mechanical defoliation. In practice, swards are mown, grazed, or both, where grazing adds treading, selective defoliation, and heterogeneous nutrient return. Whether cultivar rankings obtained under mechanical defoliation also hold under grazing, and whether mixtures perform differently than their component cultivars, are unresolved. We compared six early-heading perennial ryegrass cultivars (three diploid, three tetraploid), and three 50:50 two-cultivar mixtures. The plots were grown under three defoliation treatments (i.e., regular cutting, simulated grazing, and grazing by dairy cows), over three years at two sites. Here we show that defoliation treatment and year affected dry matter yield (DMY) and forage quality stronger than the cultivar grown. The effect of ploidy depended on the defoliation treatment. Tetraploid cultivars had slightly higher DMY under regular cutting and simulated grazing and higher metabolisable energy throughout, whereas diploid cultivars had slightly higher DMY under grazing. Simulated grazing matched the forage quality of grazed swards, including cultivar ranking, but not the cultivar ranking for DMY. Forage quality rankings can therefore be assessed through simulated grazing, whereas DMY rankings of cultivars intended for grazing require evaluation under grazing. Diploid-tetraploid mixtures were intermediate in forage quality and, under grazing, slightly higher in DMY when compared to their individual components. Evaluating cultivars and mixtures under grazing would better reflect their relative performance in the field.

papers.title: Metabolically encoded cell-surface glycoRNA remodeling enhances antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: Aberrant glycosylation reshapes tumor biology and antitumor immunity. Recently, glycoRNA has emerged as a key driver of innate immune activation, yet it remains unclear whether and how tumor cells remodel glycoRNA to elicit immune escape. Here, we systematically characterize glycoRNA signatures across breast cancer cells with distinct metabolic phenotypes and uncover metabolic reprogramming-driven remodeling of cell-surface glycoRNA landscapes. Mechanistically, glycolysis promotes c-Myc-dependent transcriptional repression of DTWD2, thereby reducing the acp3U attachment sites required for RNA glycosylation. DTWD2 loss impairs glycoRNA-mediated activation of Toll-like receptor signaling, dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell responses. Furthermore, restoration of glycoRNA by reversing aerobic glycolysis enhances the antitumor efficacy of PD-1 blockade. Clinically, we find that lower glycoRNA abundance is associated with tumor stage and unfavorable prognosis. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized route linking metabolic reprogramming to RNA glycosylation, revealing glycoRNA as a critical regulator of antitumor immunity and biomarker of tumor progression.

papers.title: Venetoclax Resistance Creates Canonical Pyroptosis Vulnerability in AML
papers.abstract: Venetoclax has transformed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) therapy, yet resistance is almost inevitable. Its diverse, often difficult-to-target drivers frequently converge on monocytic differentiation, a state that survives on MCL1 rather than BCL2. Here, we show that the very cells that escape BCL2 inhibition retain the canonical pyroptosis machinery of normal monocytes. Across 15 bulk and 4 single-cell cohorts, the canonical pyroptosis program was enriched in monocytic AML and monocytic leukemia stem cells, correlated with venetoclax resistance, and associated with inferior survival specifically after venetoclax-based therapy. In 24 cell lines and 142 patient specimens, both DPP8/9 inhibition by Val-boroPro and NLRP3 activation by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) plus nigericin preferentially killed monocytic AML cells through GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, largely sparing non-monocytic AML and lymphoid leukemias. Venetoclax preferentially depleted primitive AML blasts but enriched a monocytic residuum vulnerable to canonical pyroptosis; combining venetoclax with Val-boroPro achieved deeper ex vivo clearance than either agent alone. In venetoclax-resistant xenografts, Val-boroPro suppressed leukemia progression, and adding venetoclax further reduced leukemia burden and prolonged survival beyond either monotherapy. Thus, venetoclax resistance itself exposes an alternative, druggable cell-death program that can be therapeutically exploited to overcome this resistance.

papers.title: Natural limits on male mating sustain costly female choice, exaggerated displays, and genetic variation
papers.abstract: The persistence of costly female preferences, exaggerated male sexual displays, and the genetic variation underlying those displays remains a central puzzle in evolutionary biology. Classical Fisherian models explain preference-driven display exaggeration but not how costly preference and display can persist without runaway or collapse. These models assume that preferred males remain available regardless of previous mating success, precluding feedback through declining availability. Here I use a gene-centered analysis to show that allelic realized relatedness governs the indirect benefits of choice and that unlimited availability allows relatedness to remain high until genetic variation is lost. Individual-based simulations relaxing this idealization exposed negative feedback: as preference spread and concentrated mating success, preferred males reached capacity and became unavailable. Choosy females became less able to steer indirect fitness benefits toward additional copies of the preference allele, reducing allelic realized relatedness and constraining further evolution of preference and display. This transformed Fisherian runaway into stable exaggeration, allowing costly preference and display to persist for tens of thousands of generations across broad ranges of preference strength, mating capacity, and recombination rate. With autosomal display and a 1% viability cost of preference, stable exaggeration reached 16.5 additive-genetic standard deviations above matched no-preference baselines. Negative feedback generated disruptive selection on display, amplifying additive genetic variation beyond mutation-selection balance by as much as 32-fold, providing a resolution to the lek paradox--the persistence of display variation despite strong sexual selection--without invoking biased mutation or condition dependence. Z linkage of display loci, relevant to birds and other taxa with ZW sex determination, expanded the conditions supporting persistent preference and display, increased exaggeration, and further amplified genetic variation. Once inherent biological limits on male mating success are recognized, Fisherian sexual selection is revealed as a self-regulating form of gene-level cooperation.

papers.title: A Sense of Direction: Detecting Natural Selection Across Non-Stationary Genomes
papers.abstract: Codon substitution models detect natural selection by comparing non-synonymous (dN) and synonymous (dS) rates at each site. Standard methods assume stationary nucleotide composition across the phylogeny. In many genomes, however, GC-biased gene conversion (gBGC), codon usage bias, strand asymmetry, and host deaminases drive directional shifts in base composition along lineages. Under a stationary Muse-Gaut model with site-to-site synonymous rate variation (FEL), position-specific base frequencies and site-specific dS absorb most tree-wide drift. As a result, selection calls remain unchanged at 96%-99% of codons. At the remaining boundary sites, however, directional shifts bias dS in opposite directions depending on the ancestral codon. Rapid silent turnover at codons shifting toward the favored base inflates dS, producing apparent purifying selection and increasing across-site synonymous rate variance. Conversely, when amino acid replacements oppose the compositional tide, stationary models miss diversifying selection. Branch-specific models can accommodate shifting base frequencies, but diagonalizing a separate non-reversible codon rate matrix on every branch is too slow for large trees. Here we introduce Directional Fixed Effects Likelihood (dFEL). The method first tests whether base composition varies across taxa and runs standard FEL when frequencies are uniform. When composition shifts across lineages, dFEL roots the tree by maximum likelihood without an outgroup and models each branch as a smooth weighted average of three regime-specific transition probability matrices representing AT-enriching, neutral, and GC-enriching evolution. Sharing these matrices across the tree requires only three matrix diagonalizations per site. We validate dFEL across 1,800 simulated alignments and 87 unique empirical alignments (93 benchmark analyses) spanning up to 869 vertebrate species. It maintains calibrated false-positive rates, improves power, cuts whole-gene synonymous rate variance by up to 63%, and recovers established roots from coding sequences alone (https://github.com/veg/hyphy-3).

papers.title: A complex balance: PLETHORA - JANUS ratiometry explains the PLETHORA dosage regeneration paradox
papers.abstract: Molecular gradients are classically thought to encode positional information through concentration thresholds, but how transcription factor dosage is translated into regenerative competence remains unclear. In Arabidopsis roots, PLETHORA (PLT) transcription factors form a gradient that defines a regeneration competence zone and, following injury, rapidly re-establishes their transcriptional domain through an auto-activation. Yet, increasing PLT levels has a paradoxical effect: moderate increases expand the competence zone, whereas further increases impair regeneration. Here, combining mathematical modelling with experiments, we uncover the molecular basis of this non-monotonic response. Our model reveals that PLT activity depends not simply on its abundance, but on the balance between PLT protein complexes and unbound PLT. Following injury, PLT auto-activation rapidly restores the transcriptional domain, whereas increasing PLT dosage progressively shifts the equilibrium towards unbound PLT, reducing the availability of active PLT complexes. We identify and experimentally validate a strategy to extend regeneration competence by maintaining an appropriate ratio of PLT complexes to unbound PLT. Our findings reveal a ratiometric mechanism for decoding transcription factor dosage, in which excess regulator can attenuate rather than enhance activity. Such molecular balancing provides a mechanism by which a single transcription factor gradient can generate distinct, context-dependent outcomes during development and regeneration.

papers.title: The lymphangiogenic Ccbe1-Adamts-Vegfc axis shapes cerebrovascular regionalization via selective patterning of fenestrated vascular beds
papers.abstract: Organ development and function require regional specialization of vascular networks, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a non-canonical role for the lymphangiogenic Ccbe1-Adamts-Vegfc axis in shaping cerebrovascular regionalization in zebrafish. A ccbe1 knock-in reporter revealed highly restricted expression in the developing brain, with its genetic loss causing early vascularization defects at the pineal gland-choroid plexus interface. Simultaneous Vegfa signaling deficiency markedly exacerbated these regional vascular defects, accompanied by disrupted blood flow, local hemorrhage, and choroid plexus epithelial disorganization, while largely preserving neighboring barrier-forming vessels. Loss of vegfc closely phenocopied ccbe1 mutant defects, with fenestrated vascular patterning requiring both Vegfr2 and Vegfr3 signaling, whereas disruption of adamts3 and adamts14 indicated region-specific requirements for Vegfc-activating proteases. Conversely, pineal gland-specific overexpression of activated Vegfc partially rescued the vascularization defects. Collectively, these findings suggest that spatially restricted Ccbe1-Adamts-Vegfc activity provides angiogenic signaling specificity enabling fenestrated cerebrovascular patterning and regionalization.

papers.title: Functional genetics reveals a role for the proteasome in regulating centromere assembly
papers.abstract: Centromeres link chromosomes to spindle microtubules to direct their segregation during mitosis. The vertebrate centromere is built on two critical DNA-binding proteins, the histone H3-variant CENP-A and histone fold protein CENP-T. CENP-T is a potent scaffold for kinetochore assembly, such that concentrating it at ectopic sites is sufficient to build kinetochore-like structures. How cells prevent excess CENP-T from acting at non-centromere sites remains unclear. Here, using optical pooled screening to systematically define the requirements for CENP-A and CENP-T localization, we recover the established CENP-A deposition machinery and reveal a specific role for the proteasome in controlling CENP-T levels. We find that non-centromere CENP-T is degraded in a ubiquitin- and proteasome-dependent manner. Whereas centromere-incorporated CENP-T is stable, CENP-T that is not bound to centromeres is rapidly turned over, with the CENP-T histone fold region sufficient to confer proteasome sensitivity. Quiescent cells, which disassemble their centromeres, continue to express CENP-T but eliminate it through continuous degradation. Thus, whereas CENP-A is controlled primarily through regulated deposition, cells additionally control CENP-T by selectively degrading the unincorporated protein.

papers.title: The Genetic Discovery (GeDi) resource: Deep characterization of a multi-ancestry panel of human reference iPSCs for functional genomic studies
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are essential tools for disease modelling, drug discovery, and functional genomics, yet the field remains anchored to a small number of reference lines, limiting our understanding of how genetic background shapes cellular phenotypes across human populations. Here we describe the Genetic Discovery iPSC panel (GeDi), eight clonal iPSC lines reprogrammed from male and female donors that broadly span global human population diversity. Ancestry analysis confirmed that each line's genetic profile is concordant with donor self-reported ancestry. All GeDi lines are pluripotent and passed comprehensive quality control, demonstrating Sendai virus clearance, intact p53 pathway integrity, reproducible proliferative capacity, and compatibility with standardized genome editing workflows. Transcriptome profiling across five differentiated lineages covered 80% of annotated protein-coding genes and revealed stable donor-intrinsic variability in gene expression within each lineage. Haplotype-resolved genome assemblies were used to catalog structural variants and regions of absence of heterozygosity invisible to short-read sequencing. Whole-genome methylation analysis confirmed successful epigenetic reprogramming, catalogued the status of imprinted loci and captured the early dynamics of erosion of X chromosome inactivation (XCI) in female lines. The GeDi panel is available from The Jackson Laboratory as a quality-controlled resource designed to support functional genomic studies across varied genetic backgrounds.

papers.title: Rad53/Chk2 couples mitochondrial outputs and ROS with G2/M cell cycle progression
papers.abstract: Cell-cycle progression requires coordination with cellular metabolism, yet how checkpoint kinases contribute to this coordination during normal growth remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover an unexpected role for the checkpoint kinase Rad53/Chk2 in coupling mitochondrial and redox homeostasis to G2/M progression. In prototrophic S. cerevisiae, Rad53 loss (rad53{Delta}) disrupts cell-cycle progression and causes cells to accumulate in G2/M, alongside extensive metabolic remodelling with increased tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle flux. Mitochondrial proteomics reveals altered relative abundances of individual electron transport chain proteins, and mitochondrial membrane potential increases without increased oxygen consumption or ATP generation. This altered mitochondrial state is associated with elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidative stress. Genetic analyses establish that mitochondrial phenotypes require Rad53 kinase activity and are distinct from the loss of SML1. Antioxidant treatment rescues cell-division, budding defects and the accumulation of abnormally sized cells, establishing ROS as a primary cause of cell-cycle defects. Thus, Rad53 couples mitochondrial and redox homeostasis to G2/M progression during normal growth.

papers.title: Live imaging reveals oocyte membrane pre-remodeling forming permissive space for asymmetric division
papers.abstract: Abstract Successful oocyte maturation requires first polar body (PB1) extrusion, yet how the oocyte prepares for this asymmetric event remains unclear. Live membrane imaging of mouse oocytes reveals pronounced regional heterogeneity in plasma-membrane dynamics, generating an early polarized pattern across the surface. Whereas most of the oocyte surface and its microvilli remain relatively stable, a discrete membrane domain collapses and retracts around germinal vesicle breakdown (GVBD), separating from the zona pellucida to establish a pre-extrusion space (PES). Transient oocyte comb-like protrusions arise within the PES and subsequently collapse, converting the protrusion-filled region into an open cavity before PB1 extrusion. Mechanistically, early ERK28 dependent dissociation of the cortical scaffold ZO-1 is required for this space to form. ERK2 phosphorylates ZO-1, suppresses its phase separation, and promotes its removal from the cortex. Blocking MEK-ERK signaling prevents ZO-1 dissociation, abolishes pre-extrusion space formation, and impairs PB1 extrusion, whereas ERK activation restores these events in aged oocytes. Together, our findings identify a membrane collapse-based pre-remodeling mechanism that licenses PB1 extrusion and reveal ERK-ZO-1 signaling as a key regulator of oocyte maturation.

papers.title: Workflow and instrumentation for multiscale correlative imaging in voluminous cryogenic specimens
papers.abstract: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) enables molecular-resolution imaging of intracellular environments, but is constrained by the need to generate electron-transparent sections of the biological specimen and thus a limited imaging volume. To alleviate such limitations, we present a multiscale correlative workflow that links cryo-confocal fluorescence microscopy (cryo-FLM), cryo-focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (cryo-FIB-SEM) volume imaging (cryo-vEM), and cryo-FIB serial lamellae lift-out for cryo-ET in high-pressure frozen voluminous specimens. An integral part of this workflow is a sample holder that preserves specimen orientation across instruments, reduces manual handling, and overcomes stage-tilt limitations in cryo-FIB-SEM hardware. Applied to vitrified colorectal cancer organoids, we demonstrate that this workflow enables fluorescence-guided site preparation for cryo-vEM, which provides biological context beyond the limited field of view of cryo-ET, and targeted lift-out for fabrication of multiple lamellae from defined regions of interest. The reconstructed tomograms reveal subcellular architecture and cell-cell interfaces. This workflow establishes a modular methodological framework for continuum-resolution cryogenic imaging of complex 3D biological specimens.

papers.title: VASH1 phosphorylation regulates tubulin detyrosination via CNP/PRKG1α signaling in DRG neurons.
papers.abstract: Functional neuronal circuit formation requires precise regulation of axon growth and branching through dynamic cytoskeletal remodeling. Although microtubule detyrosination/re-tyrosination critically controls microtubule dynamics, how extracellular signals regulate this process remains unclear. Here, we identify a direct link between C-type natriuretic peptide, protein kinase cGMP-dependent 1 (CNP/cGMP/PRKG1) signaling and microtubule detyrosination in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. CNP stimulation induces growth cone enlargement, increases tyrosinated tubulin within growth cones, and reduces detyrosinated tubulin along axons, effects abolished by PRKG1 inhibition. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of the detyrosinating enzyme VASH1 phenocopies CNP-induced growth cone remodeling. In vitro kinase assays identify VASH1 as a direct PRKG1 substrate and reveal a specific C-terminal serine phosphorylation site (serine 337) that suppresses VASH1-SVBP microtubule association and detyrosination activity. Together, these findings establish VASH1-SVBP as a key downstream effector linking extracellular guidance signaling to microtubule remodeling during DRG neuronal development.

papers.title: Efferocytosis Remodels Osteoclast Metabolism and Enhances Antibacterial Defense
papers.abstract: Osteoclasts are metabolically specialized for bone resorption, but how apoptotic-cell uptake shapes their immune function remains unclear. During Staphylococcus aureus bone infection, osteoclasts engulfed apoptotic neutrophils. In osteoclast cultures, apoptotic-neutrophil exposure reduced multinucleation and resorption, induced host-defense programs, and enhanced antibacterial activity, whereas macrophages showed no comparable antibacterial response. MERTK was required for efficient osteoclast efferocytosis. Ctsk-Cre-mediated Mertk deletion increased bacterial burden and bone loss, whereas transplantation of MERTK-competent bone marrow restored osteoclast efferocytosis and reduced infection-associated bone damage. Transcriptomic and extracellular flux analyses revealed enhanced glycolytic activity and altered lactate handling in efferocytic osteoclasts. Lactate supplementation reduced osteoclast formation without reproducing the antibacterial phenotype. Inhibiting lactate production or export attenuated antibacterial activity in efferocytic osteoclasts, whereas blocking lactate uptake enhanced it. These findings identify osteoclast efferocytosis as an immune adaptation that links apoptotic-neutrophil clearance to metabolic remodeling and antibacterial defense in bone.

papers.title: Intermolecular interactions of CYP3A enzymes and cytosolic sulfotransferases (SULT1E1, SULT2A1)
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 enzymes of the CYP3A subfamily (CYP3A4 and CYP3A5) and cytosolic sulfotransferases (SULT1E1 and SULT2A1) play key roles in the sequential oxidative and conjugative metabolism of steroid hormones and xenobiotics. While their coordinated transcriptional regulation and co-expression patterns are well documented, direct physical interactions between these phase I and phase II enzymes have not previously been demonstrated. In this study, we combined systems biology analysis, SPR biosensing, activity assays, and AlphaFold2 modeling to investigate PPIs between CYP3A4/3A5 and SULT1E1/2A1. STRINGdb and transcriptomic data suggested potential associations, but direct evidence was lacking. SPR confirmed high-affinity binding (Kd 0.29-1.8 nM); the SULT2A1-CYP3A5 pair gave 0.29 nM, while SULT2A1-CYP3A4 gave 1.8 nM. Notably, the presence of the sulfo group donor SULT PAPS, had minimal effect on binding affinity. Functional assays demonstrated that SULTs slightly inhibited CYP3A4 activity while moderately enhancing CYP3A5 activity in the presence of SULT1E1, both with and without PAPS, whereas the addition of CYPs leads to selectively increase in SULT2A1 activity in vitro by 38% (CYP3A4) and 108% (CYP3A5), without affecting SULT1E1. AlphaFold2 models revealed stable interfaces (715-1856 square angstroms) with 10-16 H-bonds and salt bridges. The results of our in silico tunnel analysis suggested a plausible alignment of substrate exit channels from CYPs with entry pathways to SULTs, supporting a mechanistic basis for substrate channeling in CYP-SULT complexes. These results indicate that the enzymes may form functional multienzyme complexes, offering new insights into coordinated steroid/xenobiotic metabolism and drug clearance.

papers.title: Selection of DNA aptamers targeting PirAB toxin for potential biosensing applications in acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease (AHPND)
papers.abstract: The timely detection of AHPND is one of the key factors to avoid the great economic losses that this disease entails for aquaculture. The use of aptamers as detection tools allows us to develop a method focused on the specific needs of the producer, such as simple and easy to use, ability to carry out a safe and rapid response field detection. Vibrio parahaemolyticus is currently known as the main causal agent of AHPND in shrimp cultures, however, it is not limited to this species as a transfer of virulence factors has been observed, including the genes encoding the PirAB binary toxin. The concern that this transfer implies has led us to focus our interest on the PirAB binary toxin as a ligand for the development of aptamers capable of identifying it in the field in early stages and avoiding advanced stages of the disease, giving the producer the ability to take preventive actions and reduce the risk of losses. In the present work we have optimized the SELEX (systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment) aptamer development methodology to rapidly develop candidates capable of detecting both the PirAB complex and its subunits separately, obtaining candidates with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 65 to 700 nM for the PirB subunit and 1 to 3 uM for the PirAB complex. These aptamers provide the first step toward the development of a rapid detection method targeting the causative toxin of AHPND and aid in a new user-friendly approach to early disease detection.

papers.title: KDM4 inhibition alters H3K9me3 distribution and developmental responses in SETDB1-deficient embryonic stem cells
papers.abstract: SETDB1 contributes to histone H3 lysine 9 methylation, whereas KDM4 demethylases act on H3K9 and, for KDM4A-C, H3K36. We examined whether Setdb1 status modifies responses to the KDM4-family inhibitor QC6352 in embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryoid bodies (EBs). QC6352 shifted Setdb1-depleted ESC colonies toward more compact morphology and increased alkaline-phosphatase (AP) staining, but also affected Setdb1-intact cells. Separate Kdm4a, Kdm4b, and Kdm4c knockdowns identified overlapping and member-specific transcriptional responses. Factorial RNA-seq revealed broadly concordant transcriptional responses to KDM4 inhibition in Setdb1-intact and depleted ESCs, alongside a smaller subset of genes with genotype-dependent treatment effects. Within this subset, two gene modules showed attenuation or reversal of Setdb1-associated expression changes following KDM4 inhibition. ChIP-seq revealed changes in the relative distribution of H3K9me3, H3K36me3, and H3K4me3 between promoters and gene bodies following KDM4 inhibition. KDM4 inhibition altered H3K9me3 distributions across repeat families in both Setdb1-intact and depleted ESCs. QC6352 also altered EB morphology and produced transcriptional responses that differed between ESCs and EBs. These findings show that KDM4 inhibition remodels chromatin and transcription in both Setdb1-intact and depleted ESCs, with Setdb1 status influencing a subset of transcriptional responses.

papers.title: Guanine content in the CTCF motif encodes a vulnerability to persistent, alcohol-induced redistribution
papers.abstract: Alcohol consumption is a leading contributor to the global disease burden, yet its molecular consequences remain incompletely understood. Ethanols first metabolite, acetaldehyde, modifies guanine to form DNA adducts and DNA-protein crosslinks that block elongating RNA polymerase II. Because acetaldehyde acts specifically on guanine, we hypothesized that chromatin features would be disrupted in a sequence-dependent rather than stochastic manner. Here we confirm that alcohol exposure displaces elongating RNA polymerase II (RNAPIIs2p) from gene bodies, relocating to promoters. In addition to this confirmation, we found that RNAPIIs2p also relocates to discrete guanine-rich intergenic CTCF sites. Loci with high guanine content at the CTCF motifs zinc finger 5 (ZF5) binding position showed the largest increase in both CTCF and cohesin (RAD21), with CTCF occupancy changes persisting even six days after alcohol withdrawal. Surprisingly, using Hi-C, we found that these changes to CTCF and cohesin do not impact the pronounced structural CTCF loops, but are instead primarily associated with altered guanine-rich enhancer-promoter contacts that connect to lasting changes to gene expression. Beyond our cell-line model, the same sequence rule accounts for altered CTCF occupancy in a mouse starvation (metabolic stress) model and in the placentae after paternal alcohol exposure. Together these findings link alcohol exposure to sequence-directed changes to chromatin whose rules are conserved in alcohol-associated disease.

papers.title: Distinct roles of Hsp110 proteins in regulating prion propagation
papers.abstract: Prion diseases are fatal, transmissible neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the conformational conversion of the cellular prion protein (PrPC) into its pathogenic isoform PrPSc. Propagation of prions depends on the fragmentation of PrPSc aggregates to generate new seeds. However, the factors regulating this process remain incompletely understood. For yeast prions, Hsp104 that has no mammalian homologue, is firmly established as a disaggregase. Hsp110 has emerged as a potential mediator of protein disaggregation and aggregate remodeling in mammalian cells. Although Hsp110 proteins have been implicated in several protein misfolding disorders, their individual contributions to mammalian prion propagation have not been characterized. In this study, we examined the roles of the three Hsp110 proteins -Apg-1, Apg-2, and Hsp105- in cellular prion infection. CRISPR-generated knockout cell lines were established for each Hsp110 and evaluated for their effect on de novo prion infection. PrPSc accumulation was assessed by immunoblot across serial passages and up to 40 days, and prion seeding activity was quantified using real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC). Loss of individual Hsp110s produced distinct effects on prion propagation. Apg-1-deficient cells exhibited strongly reduced levels of PrPSc over all passages analyzed, suggesting a role for Apg-1 in establishing persistent prion infection. Interestingly, prion seeding activity was detectable in later passages. Hsp105-deficient cells displayed reduced PrPSc levels during the early stages, indicating that Hsp105 contributes to early prion replication. In contrast, Apg-2 knockout resulted in high prion seeding activity over all passages analyzed and only slightly reduced PrPSc levels in early passages. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Hsp110 family members perform distinct functions during early phases of prion infection and establishment of persistent infection. This work provides new insight into the role of molecular chaperones in prion biology and identifies Hsp110 proteins as potential modulators of prion replication and potentially therapeutic targets for protein misfolding diseases.

papers.title: Disruption of the polyuracil tract can greatly enhance immunostimulatory properties of influenza delVGs
papers.abstract: Non-standard viral genomes (nsVGs) are replication-incompetent genomes within viral populations whose presence has been associated with an enhanced immune response. This association has garnered interest in their use as potential antivirals, vaccine adjuvants, or general immune-modulators. In influenza A virus (IAV), the predominant nsVG is a large deletion in one of the three polymerase segments, which results in deletion-containing viral genomes (delVGs). Work from our group has found that individual delVGs can be recovered that are capable of stimulating high levels of interferon, however we and others have not previously found any consistent means of predicting or modifying determinants of this stimulation. Using high-throughput genetic approaches, we find that specific mutations disrupting the polyuracil tract in IAV delVGs can enhance interferon production by up to two orders of magnitude. Such variants can also associate with improved rescue in artificial systems engineered to exclude infectious virus, and can greatly suppress the growth of replication-competent virus. These findings indicate the polyuracil tract is a key, and unexpected, target for improvement of immunostimulatory delVGs derived from IAV.

papers.title: Longitudinal Metaproteomic and Lysine Crotonylation Remodeling Defines Clinical Response to Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Ulcerative Colitis
papers.abstract: Background Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) can induce steroid-free clinical remission in a subset of patients with ulcerative colitis (UC), but treatment responses remain heterogeneous and are not fully explained by taxonomic microbiome shifts. To define functional molecular features associated with FMT efficacy, we performed integrated longitudinal fecal metaproteomic and lysine crotonylation (Kcr) profiling. Methods We analyzed 87 fecal samples from 23 patients with active UC collected at baseline and at weeks 1, 8, and 12 after FMT. Patients were classified as responders (n = 13) or non-responders (n = 10) according to steroid-free clinical remission at week 12. Across samples, we identified an average of 3,682 proteins and 562 Kcr sites per sample. Results Responders showed greater metaproteomic and meta-crotonylomic complexity at week 12, sustained enrichment of Prevotella and Faecalibacterium, and eight directionally consistent baseline-altered proteins with candidate prognostic value. After FMT, responders exhibited coordinated microbial functional remodeling, including increased proteins involved in short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolism, acyl-CoA-centered pathways, nutrient transport, and polysaccharide degradation, together with attenuation of host neutrophil-related inflammatory protein and Kcr signatures. Non-responders showed minimal or opposing molecular changes. Conclusions: These findings nominate longitudinal fecal metaproteomic and Kcr remodeling as functional molecular readouts of clinical response to FMT in UC and highlight lysine crotonylation as an underexplored metabolite-sensitive layer linking microbial metabolic restoration with host inflammatory resolution.
